hypothesis: For a fixed baseline detector trained on non-adversarial data, a systematic red-teaming loop that (a) generates diverse watermark-removal attacks spanning heuristic, optimization-based, and generative pipelines, and (b) incorporates the hardest successful attacks via adversarial training and hard negative mining, will measurably reduce attack evasion rates at a fixed false-positive rate, without materially degrading clean-image performance.

baseline.description: Baseline detector performance against a standardized suite of watermark-removal attacks, using the best image-based detector from previous chapters without any attack-aware training.
baseline.evaluation_protocol: Evaluate the frozen baseline detector on a held-out test set of watermarked images and their attacked variants generated by pre-defined attack pipelines. No model updates or hard negative mining.
attacks_in_scope: Heuristic transforms: crops, rescaling, JPEG recompression, Gaussian blur, color jitter.
Simple resynthesis: low-strength style transfer, upsample-downsample via standard super-resolution model.
Generative edits: single-pass diffusion-based inpainting or prompt-edit using off-the-shelf diffusion model with default safety settings.

treatment.description: Detector retrained (or fine-tuned) with adversarial examples produced by the same attack suite under a structured red-teaming workflow, including hard negative mining from those attacks that successfully evade the baseline.

adversarial_training_procedure.phase_1_seed_attacks: Run all baseline attacks on a slice of the training watermarked images to generate candidate adversarial examples.
adversarial_training_procedure.phase_2_hard_negative_mining: Identify attacks where the baseline detector predicts 'no removal' or low risk for images with ground-truth 'watermark removed'. Select top-K most confident false negatives per attack family.
adversarial_training_procedure.phase_3_finetuning: Fine-tune the baseline detector on the union of original training data and mined hard negatives, with class rebalancing and possibly higher loss weights for adversarially removed samples.
adversarial_training_procedure.phase_4_re-evaluation: Re-evaluate the updated detector on the same standardized attack testbed and on the clean/benign test data to check for regressions.

constant_factors_vs_baseline: Same model architecture and input pre-processing.
Same clean training data as baseline (treatment adds extra adversarial examples).
Same evaluation datasets and metrics for comparability.
Same inference-time configuration (batch size, thresholds, preprocessing).

workloads.name: clean_reference_eval
workloads.description: Measure detector performance on a clean, held-out test set of watermarked and non-watermarked images with no attack applied.
steps: Load frozen detector checkpoint (baseline or treatment).
Compute confusion matrix for classes: {clean, watermarked, watermark-removed} (or corresponding binary tasks, depending on chapter 6 design).
Log metrics and store per-example predictions for later analysis.
workloads.purpose: Establish reference performance and ensure adversarial training does not meaningfully degrade clean performance.

workloads.name: heuristic_attack_eval
workloads.description: Evaluate detector robustness to deterministic content-preserving transforms that may degrade or remove watermark signal.
workloads.evaluation: For each attack pipeline, generate attacked images from the watermarked test split and evaluate evasion rates (fraction of originally correctly-flagged images that become misclassified or predicted as low-risk).

workloads.name: optimization_based_attack_eval
workloads.description: Use gradient- or query-based optimization procedures (parameterized within the repository) to search for minimal watermark-removal perturbations under perceptual constraints.

transform_sequence: Iterative update: x_{t+1} = Proj_Perceived(x_t + alpha * sign(grad_loss)), constrained by LPIPS(x_t, x0) <= epsilon_lpips.
Optional: mixed with JPEG + blur at every N steps.
SquareAttack-like random block perturbations respecting perceptual budget.
Keep perturbation if it reduces predicted removal probability below threshold.

workloads.evaluation: Compute attack success (evasion) conditioned on respecting perceptual bounds, and compare baseline vs. treatment detectors.

workloads.name: generative_attack_eval
workloads.description: Stress-test the detector with generative resynthesis and diffusion-based edits aimed at washing out watermark traces while preserving semantics.

transform_sequence: Super-resolve using pretrained SR model (e.g., ESRGAN variant) to original resolution.
Apply inpainting or full-image resynthesis with guidance scale and steps configured to preserve coarse layout.

workloads.evaluation: Estimate how often generative transformations cause the detector to miss watermark removal, and measure perceptual similarity to original images.

workloads.name: adversarial_training_loop
workloads.description: Full red-teaming loop combining attack generation, hard negative mining, and training updates.
steps: Sample a subset of watermarked training images (e.g., 20–30%).

Apply all defined attack pipelines from heuristic_attack_eval, optimization_based_attack_eval, and generative_attack_eval in batched mode using training-time attack configs (can be slightly lighter weight than evaluation attacks).
Run baseline detector on these attacked samples.
Select hard negatives: attacked images where the baseline detector predicts 'no removal' or low removal probability despite known removal ground truth.
Create augmented training set by unioning original training samples with a capped number (e.g., up to N per original) of hard negatives per attack family.
Fine-tune detector using this combined dataset, tracking validation performance on a clean dev set and an adversarial dev set.
Persist updated checkpoint and logs for later comparison.
workloads.purpose: Produce the treatment model and quantify the gains from adversarial training and hard negative mining.

randomness.note: Optimization-based attacks may still have minor nondeterminism on GPU; seed is set to minimize but not fully eliminate it.

data_splits.immutability: Splits must not be modified across baseline vs. treatment; any filtering (e.g., for optimization attacks) must be via deterministic index lists stored under artifacts/splits/.

model_architecture.name: image_cnn_detector_v1
model_architecture.constraint: Exactly the same architecture and hyperparameters between baseline and treatment; the only change is inclusion of adversarial examples in training.

preprocessing.normalization: Mean/std normalization as defined in configs/preprocessing/image_v1.yaml
preprocessing.note: Attack pipelines operate on the same canonical preprocessed images or on their unnormalized counterparts, as specified in the attack config, but final detector input must pass through the standard preprocessing.

evaluation_thresholds.calibration_method: Fixed threshold determined on clean dev set before attacks; must be held fixed when comparing baseline vs. treatment under attack.

metrics.name: clean_auroc
metrics.description: Area under ROC curve for detecting watermark removal on the clean held-out test set.

metrics.name: clean_f1
metrics.description: F1 score on clean test data at the primary_decision_threshold.

metrics.name: attack_evasion_rate
metrics.description: For a given attack family and detector, the fraction of examples that were correctly flagged as watermark-removed in their original form but are incorrectly classified or predicted as low-risk after attack.

metrics.name: attack_success_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of attempted attacks that both (a) respect the specified perceptual constraint and (b) cause misclassification or low-risk prediction by the detector.

metrics.name: perceptual_distance_lpips
metrics.description: Average LPIPS distance between original and attacked images per attack type on the test set.

metrics.name: psnr
metrics.description: Average Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio between original and attacked images per attack type.

metrics.name: adv_auroc
metrics.description: AUROC on the union of clean and adversarially attacked images, treating all attacked watermarked images as positive for 'removal or tampering'.

metrics.name: adv_f1
metrics.description: F1 score on the union of clean and adversarially attacked images at the primary_decision_threshold.

metrics.name: avg_query_count
metrics.description: For query-based optimization attacks, mean number of detector queries per successfully attacked image.

metrics.name: training_time
metrics.description: Wall-clock GPU hours for baseline and treatment training runs, measured separately.

metrics.name: attack_gen_time
metrics.description: Approximate GPU hours spent generating adversarial examples for the adversarial training loop.

primary.description: Reduced attack evasion rate after adversarial training with minimal degradation on clean data.
primary.formal_condition: For each major attack family A in {heuristic, optimization, generative}, attack_evasion_rate_treatment(A) <= 0.7 * attack_evasion_rate_baseline(A), and clean_auroc_treatment >= clean_auroc_baseline - 0.02.

secondary.description: Preserved or improved F1 score on clean data at fixed operating point.

governance_notes: Any gain in attack robustness that induces more than a 3–5 percentage point drop in clean F1 should be flagged as potentially unacceptable for production and discussed with policy/compliance counterparts.
Optimization-based attacks that significantly exceed predefined perceptual distance thresholds should be analyzed qualitatively and may be excluded from headline metrics but still documented.

failure_modes.name: overfitting_to_known_attacks
failure_modes.description: Treatment model shows strong improvement against exactly the attack pipelines used for training but fails to generalize to slightly varied or unseen attack parameters.
indicators: Large gains in attack_evasion_rate for training-time attack configs but negligible gains for held-out parameters or unseen attack variants.
adv_auroc improves on in-distribution adversarial dev set but not on separate adversarial test set.
mitigations: Include parametric variation within each attack family when generating training adversarial examples.
Reserve at least one unseen attack configuration per family exclusively for final evaluation.

failure_modes.name: clean_performance_collapse
failure_modes.description: Adversarial training harms performance on clean and benign content.
mitigations: Reduce the proportion of adversarial examples in each training minibatch.
Use separate loss weights for clean vs. adversarial data.
Early stop using clean dev set metrics as primary criteria.

failure_modes.name: attack_pipeline_instability
failure_modes.description: Nondeterminism or version drift in generative/diffusion models leads to irreproducible results.
indicators: Repeated runs with same seed and config produce different attack_success_rate > small tolerance.
Minor library or model version changes produce large metric shifts.
mitigations: Pin model checkpoints and library versions in environment definition.
Cache generated adversarial examples with content hashes and use them for final evaluation.
Log full attack configuration, including random seeds and prompts, in structured metadata.

failure_modes.name: unrealistic_attack_sampling
failure_modes.description: Attack configurations are either too weak (trivially detectable) or too strong (resulting in visually implausible images or obvious artifacts).
indicators: Very low perceptual_distance_lpips for almost all attacks but also low attack_success_rate.
Very high LPIPS / low PSNR, or human raters deem images clearly corrupted.
Optimization attacks consistently hit constraint bounds.
mitigations: Tune perceptual constraints using small pilot studies, including manual inspection.
Calibrate LPIPS/PSNR thresholds to approximate 'imperceptible or minimally noticeable' perturbations.
Document and possibly exclude attacks that do not meet agreed realism criteria.

failure_modes.name: resource_exhaustion
failure_modes.description: Optimization-based and diffusion-based attacks consume excessive compute, making the experiment impractical.
indicators: attack_gen_time exceeds planned budget (e.g., >2x baseline training_time).
GPU out-of-memory errors or timeouts during batched attack generation.
mitigations: Subsample test set for the most expensive attacks and clearly record sampling.
Reduce diffusion steps or optimization iterations while tracking effect on perceptual metrics and attack_success_rate.
Use mixed precision and smaller image sizes if consistent with prior chapters.

storage.note: Includes space for base datasets, generated adversarial datasets, model checkpoints, and logs.

software.os: Linux (Ubuntu 20.04 or later recommended); macOS may work but is not primary test target.
key_python_packages: diffusers (for diffusion-based attacks; pinned version as per env file)
software.reproducibility: Use the provided environment file and do not upgrade core ML libraries independently. Run on a single GPU process with fixed seeds.

run_instructions: 1. Clone the repository and set up environment
# Create and activate environment (example with conda)
2. Prepare datasets (if not already built from Chapter 4)
# Optionally, pre-generate a smaller subset for expensive optimization attacks
3. Ensure baseline detector checkpoint is available
# Train baseline if not already done (see Chapter 6)
# Or download/preload a reference checkpoint as documented in the repo README
5. Run adversarial training with hard negative mining
6. Re-run evaluations with the adversarially trained detector
# Optionally, render governance-oriented plots/tables for Chapter 12 use

fields.image_id: string; stable identifier linking to original dataset sample.
fields.attack_config_hash: string; hash of attack configuration dict to ensure reproducibility.
fields.detector_checkpoint_path: string; path to model weights used.
fields.prediction_score: float; model score for 'watermark removed/tampered' class.
fields.is_correct: boolean; whether predicted_label == true_label under evaluation label mapping.
fields.lpips_distance: float|null; LPIPS between original and attacked, null for 'none' attack.
fields.psnr: float|null; PSNR between original and attacked, null for 'none' attack.
fields.num_queries: integer|null; number of model queries used for this attack if applicable.
fields.runtime_ms: integer; end-to-end inference or attack+inference time in milliseconds.
fields.timestamp: string; ISO 8601 timestamp when record was generated.

fields.attack_ids: array[string]; list of attack IDs included in this aggregate.
fields.adv_auroc: float; AUROC on combined clean+attacked set for this run_type and attack_family.
fields.adv_f1: float; F1 on combined clean+attacked set at primary_decision_threshold.
fields.mean_lpips_distance: float|null; average LPIPS across attacked samples if applicable.
fields.mean_psnr: float|null; average PSNR across attacked samples if applicable.
fields.mean_num_queries: float|null; average number of queries per sample for query-based attacks.

confidence_intervals.attack_evasion_rate_95_ci: array[float,float]|null; lower and upper bounds if bootstrapped.

config_refs.model_config_path: string; path to model config file.
config_refs.attack_config_paths: array[string]; list of attack config paths used.
config_refs.eval_config_path: string; path to evaluation config file.

fields.notes: string; free-text commentary (e.g., anomaly flags or deviations).

fields.treatment_checkpoint: string; path to adversarially trained detector.

success_criteria_evaluation.details: string; explanation of which criteria passed/failed with references to metrics.

governance_summary.clean_performance_change: string; human-readable summary of any regressions on clean data.
governance_summary.robustness_change: string; summary of robustness improvements or regressions.
governance_summary.flagged_failure_modes: array[string]; names of any triggered failure modes.
